3	## Scope and interface
4	
5	Worker owns only `linkvault/server.py`, `tests/test_server.py`, and these notes. T3 runs concurrently in disjoint files. No CLI/client, frozen artifact, board, handoff or shared fixture changes; no commits.
6	
7	`server.run(args)` consumes `db, admin_key, port, rate_limit, fake_clock`; `fake_clock` is the T1/T3-agreed parsed integer seconds or `None`. It returns 3 on database initialization/bind failure and 0 on clean signal shutdown. `Server` is a loopback-only ThreadingHTTPServer with file-local in-process HTTP fixtures. `Handler` routes using the original request line rather than normalized `self.path`, handles arbitrary extension methods via JSON route errors, applies route/auth/rate/size/JSON/validation/state precedence and shares T1 storage/clock/limiter.
8	
9	## Unicode Location wire decision
10	
11	Valid URLs are not restricted beyond T1 R6 validation. Storage and JSON retain the original URL. For redirect Location, original Latin-1-compatible values use their original Latin-1 bytes (preserving stdlib header compatibility); values containing non-Latin-1 characters use the original value's UTF-8 bytes, emitted through the stdlib header writer without percent escaping, IDNA, normalization, or replacement. A client that decodes every header as Latin-1 must recover the raw octets and decode UTF-8 for this latter case. The contract does not specify a Unicode header charset. Focused regression tests inspect raw header bytes for ASCII, Latin-1, and CJK URLs, including Unicode hosts/paths/queries/fragments.
12	
13	## Lifecycle design and validation scope
14	
15	Signals set only a main-thread boolean. A separate thread serves; the main thread stops acceptance with shutdown(), interrupts every accepted active socket (including idle, partial headers, and incomplete bodies), joins non-daemon handler threads, then closes storage and restores signal handlers. No DB operation may outlive closure. Focused tests invoke run on the main thread with real in-process signals and local sockets; subprocess CLI/OS exit and restart acceptance remain T4 responsibility. SIGBREAK is conditionally tested and skipped when absent.

17	All local runtime evidence uses available Python 3.9.6 and is below-target evidence, not supported Python >=3.11 proof. No installs. Whole-package `python -m compileall -q linkvault` is deliberately pending the parent quiescent barrier after both parallel workers return; not claimed passed. 1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

14	class APIError(Exception):
15	    """An expected API failure; unexpected exceptions remain internal errors."""
16	
17	    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str, headers: dict | None = None):
18	        super().__init__(message)
19	        self.status = status
20	        self.code = code
21	        self.message = message
22	        self.headers = {} if headers is None else headers

24	    def body(self) -> dict:
25	        return {"error": {"code": self.code, "message": self.message}}

27	
28	def json_bytes(value: object) -> bytes:
29	    return json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True).encode("utf-8")
30	
31	
32	def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
33	    raise ValueError("Non-JSON number: " + value)
34	
35	
36	def decode_json(body: bytes) -> dict:
37	    """Decode an object only; request size/auth/route checks belong to HTTP."""
38	    try:
39	        value = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"), parse_constant=_reject_constant)
40	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
41	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_json", "Expected a UTF-8 JSON object") from None
42	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
43	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_json", "Expected a JSON object")
44	    return value

46	
47	_EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
48	_TIMESTAMP = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z")
49	_SLUG = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}")
50	
51	
52	def parse_timestamp(value: str) -> int:
53	    if not isinstance(value, str) or _TIMESTAMP.fullmatch(value) is None:
54	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp")
55	    try:
56	        instant = datetime(
57	            int(value[:4]), int(value[5:7]), int(value[8:10]),
58	            int(value[11:13]), int(value[14:16]), int(value[17:19]),
59	            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
60	        )
61	    except ValueError:
62	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp") from None
63	    return (instant - _EPOCH) // timedelta(seconds=1)
64	
65	
66	def format_timestamp(value: int) -> str:
67	    instant = _EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=value)
68	    return (
69	        f"{instant.year:04d}-{instant.month:02d}-{instant.day:02d}"
70	        f"T{instant.hour:02d}:{instant.minute:02d}:{instant.second:02d}Z"
71	    )

76	    return isinstance(value, str) and _SLUG.fullmatch(value) is not None

81	        not isinstance(value, str) or not value or len(value) > 2048
82	        or any(character.isspace() or ord(character) < 0x21 or ord(character) == 0x7F
83	               for character in value)

118	class Clock:
119	    """None selects real time; fake_now and set() use parsed integer seconds."""
120	
121	    def __init__(self, fake_now: int | None = None):
122	        self._fake_now = fake_now
123	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
124	        self.is_fake = fake_now is not None
125	
126	    def now(self) -> int:
127	        with self._lock:
128	            return self._fake_now if self.is_fake else math.floor(time.time())
129	
130	    def set(self, now: int) -> int:
131	        with self._lock:
132	            if not self.is_fake:
133	                raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Fake clock is disabled")
134	            self._fake_now = now
135	            return now

138	class RateLimiter:
139	    """Count every check, retaining historical windows for backward fake time."""
140	
141	    def __init__(self, limit: int = 60):
142	        if type(limit) is not int or limit < 1:
143	            raise ValueError("Rate limit must be a positive integer")
144	        self._limit = limit
145	        self._counts: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
146	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
147	
148	    def check(self, token_hash: str, now: int) -> None:
149	        window_start = now - now % 60
150	        key = (token_hash, window_start)
151	        with self._lock:
152	            count = self._counts.get(key, 0) + 1
153	            self._counts[key] = count
154	        if count > self._limit:
155	            raise APIError(
156	                429, "rate_limited", "Rate limit exceeded",
157	                {"Retry-After": str(window_start + 60 - now)},
158	            )

3	## Scope and interface
4	
5	Worker owns only `linkvault/server.py`, `tests/test_server.py`, and these notes. T3 runs concurrently in disjoint files. No CLI/client, frozen artifact, board, handoff or shared fixture changes; no commits.
6	
7	`server.run(args)` consumes `db, admin_key, port, rate_limit, fake_clock`; `fake_clock` is the T1/T3-agreed parsed integer seconds or `None`. It returns 3 on database initialization/bind failure and 0 on clean signal shutdown. `Server` is a loopback-only ThreadingHTTPServer with file-local in-process HTTP fixtures. `Handler` routes using the original request line rather than normalized `self.path`, handles arbitrary extension methods via JSON route errors, applies route/auth/rate/size/JSON/validation/state precedence and shares T1 storage/clock/limiter.
8	
9	## Unicode Location wire decision
10	
11	Valid URLs are not restricted beyond T1 R6 validation. Storage and JSON retain the original URL. For redirect Location, original Latin-1-compatible values use their original Latin-1 bytes (preserving stdlib header compatibility); values containing non-Latin-1 characters use the original value's UTF-8 bytes, emitted through the stdlib header writer without percent escaping, IDNA, normalization, or replacement. A client that decodes every header as Latin-1 must recover the raw octets and decode UTF-8 for this latter case. The contract does not specify a Unicode header charset. Focused regression tests inspect raw header bytes for ASCII, Latin-1, and CJK URLs, including Unicode hosts/paths/queries/fragments.
12	
13	## Lifecycle design and validation scope
14	
15	Signals set only a main-thread boolean. A separate thread serves; the main thread stops acceptance with shutdown(), interrupts every accepted active socket (including idle, partial headers, and incomplete bodies), joins non-daemon handler threads, then closes storage and restores signal handlers. No DB operation may outlive closure. Focused tests invoke run on the main thread with real in-process signals and local sockets; subprocess CLI/OS exit and restart acceptance remain T4 responsibility. SIGBREAK is conditionally tested and skipped when absent.

17	All local runtime evidence uses available Python 3.9.6 and is below-target evidence, not supported Python >=3.11 proof. No installs. Whole-package `python -m compileall -q linkvault` is deliberately pending the parent quiescent barrier after both parallel workers return; not claimed passed. 1	"""Argument parsing and lazy server/client dispatch."""
2	
3	import argparse
4	import os
5	
6	from .domain import APIError, parse_timestamp
7	
8	
9	def _nonempty(value):
10	    if not value:
11	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must not be empty")
12	    return value
13	
14	
15	def _port(value):
16	    number = int(value)
17	    if not 0 <= number <= 65535:
18	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be between 0 and 65535")
19	    return number
20	
21	
22	def _rate_limit(value):
23	    number = int(value)
24	    if number < 1:
25	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be at least 1")
26	    return number
27	
28	
29	def _timestamp(value):
30	    try:
31	        return parse_timestamp(value)
32	    except APIError as error:
33	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(error.message) from None
34	
35	
36	def _client_options(parser):
37	    # Suppressed defaults preserve options supplied before the token create leaf.
38	    parser.add_argument("--server", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
39	    parser.add_argument("--token", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
40	
41	
42	def _parser():
43	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="linkvault")
44	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
45	
46	    serve = commands.add_parser("serve")
47	    serve.add_argument("--db", required=True)
48	    serve.add_argument("--admin-key", required=True, type=_nonempty)
49	    serve.add_argument("--port", type=_port, default=8000)
50	    serve.add_argument("--rate-limit", type=_rate_limit, default=60)
51	    serve.add_argument("--fake-clock", type=_timestamp)
52	
53	    token = commands.add_parser("token")
54	    _client_options(token)
55	    token_commands = token.add_subparsers(dest="token_command", required=True)
56	    create = token_commands.add_parser("create")
57	    _client_options(create)
58	    create.add_argument("--admin-key", required=True, type=_nonempty)
59	
60	    shorten = commands.add_parser("shorten")
61	    _client_options(shorten)
62	    shorten.add_argument("url")
63	    shorten.add_argument("--slug")
64	    shorten.add_argument("--expires-in", type=int)
65	
66	    listing = commands.add_parser("list")
67	    _client_options(listing)
68	    for name in ("stats", "delete"):
69	        command = commands.add_parser(name)
70	        _client_options(command)
71	        command.add_argument("slug")
72	    return parser
73	
74	
75	def main(argv=None):
76	    parser = _parser()
77	    try:
78	        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
79	        if args.command != "serve":
80	            args.server = getattr(args, "server", os.environ.get("LINKVAULT_SERVER"))
81	            args.token = getattr(args, "token", os.environ.get("LINKVAULT_TOKEN"))
82	            if not args.server:
83	                parser.error("--server or LINKVAULT_SERVER is required")
84	            if args.command != "token" and not args.token:
85	                parser.error("--token or LINKVAULT_TOKEN is required")
86	    except SystemExit as error:
87	        return error.code
88	
89	    if args.command == "serve":
90	        from . import server
91	
92	        return server.run(args)
93	
94	    from . import client
95	
96	    return client.run(args)
97

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import hashlib
6	import re
7	import secrets
8	import sqlite3
9	import threading
10	
11	from .domain import APIError, format_timestamp, validate_create
12	
13	
14	_SCHEMA = """
15	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
16	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
17	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
18	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
19	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
20	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
21	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
22	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
23	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
24	  expires_at INTEGER,
25	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
26	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
27	"""
28	_ALPHABET = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
29	_TOKEN = re.compile(r"lv_[0-9a-f]{32}")
30	
31	
32	def _digest(token: str) -> str:
33	    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
34	
35	
36	def _link(row: sqlite3.Row, base_url: str) -> dict:
37	    return {
38	        "slug": row["slug"],
39	        "url": row["url"],
40	        "short_url": f"{base_url}/{row['slug']}",
41	        "created_at": format_timestamp(row["created_at"]),
42	        "expires_at": (format_timestamp(row["expires_at"])
43	                       if row["expires_at"] is not None else None),
44	        "clicks": row["clicks"],
45	        "last_clicked_at": (format_timestamp(row["last_clicked_at"])
46	                            if row["last_clicked_at"] is not None else None),
47	    }
48	
49	
50	class Storage:
51	    def __init__(self, path: str):
52	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
53	        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
54	        with self._lock:
55	            try:
56	                self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
57	                self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
58	                self._conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
59	                self._conn.commit()
60	            except Exception:
61	                self._conn.close()
62	                raise
63	
64	    def close(self) -> None:
65	        with self._lock:
66	            self._conn.close()
67	
68	    def issue_token(self, now: int) -> dict:
69	        token = "lv_" + secrets.token_hex(16)

57	def check_wire(status, headers, body):
58	    assert headers["Content-Length"] == str(len(body))
59	    if body:
60	        assert headers["Content-Type"] == "application/json"
61	        value = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
62	        assert body == encode(value)
63	        if status >= 400:
64	            assert list(value) == ["error"]
65	            assert list(value["error"]) == ["code", "message"]
66	    return status, headers, body

74	class Process:
75	    def __init__(self, directory, db, rate_limit, fake_clock):
76	        self.db = db
77	        self.stderr_path = directory / "server.stderr"
78	        self.stderr_file = self.stderr_path.open("wb")
79	        arguments = [sys.executable, "-m", "linkvault", "serve", "--db", str(db),
80	                     "--admin-key", ADMIN_KEY, "--port", "0",
81	                     "--rate-limit", str(rate_limit)]
82	        if fake_clock is not None:
83	            arguments += ["--fake-clock", fake_clock]
84	        options = {"creationflags": subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP} if os.name == "nt" else {}
85	        self.process = subprocess.Popen(arguments, cwd=ROOT, env=environment(),
86	                                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=self.stderr_file,
87	                                        **options)
88	        self.lines = []
89	        ready = queue.Queue()
90	
91	        def read_stdout():
92	            for line in iter(self.process.stdout.readline, b""):
93	                self.lines.append(line)
94	                ready.put(line)
95	            ready.put(b"")
96	
97	        self.reader = threading.Thread(target=read_stdout, daemon=True)
98	        self.reader.start()
99	        try:
100	            # No -u/PYTHONUNBUFFERED: receipt while alive proves readiness flush.
101	            self.ready_line = ready.get(timeout=5)
102	            match = re.fullmatch(rb"LISTENING (http://127\.0\.0\.1:([0-9]+))\r?\n",
103	                                 self.ready_line)
104	            assert match, (self.ready_line, self.stderr_path.read_bytes())
105	            self.url = match[1].decode("ascii")
106	            self.port = int(match[2])
107	            assert 1 <= self.port <= 65535
108	            assert self.process.poll() is None
109	        except BaseException:
110	            self.process.kill()
111	            self.process.wait(timeout=5)
112	            self.reader.join(timeout=2)
113	            self.process.stdout.close()
114	            self.stderr_file.close()
115	            raise
116	
117	    def call(self, method, path, body=None, headers=None):
118	        # http.client never follows redirects.
119	        connection = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.port, timeout=5)
120	        try:
121	            connection.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers or {})
122	            response = connection.getresponse()
123	            return check_wire(response.status, dict(response.getheaders()), response.read())
124	        finally:
125	            connection.close()
126	
127	    def raw(self, method, path, headers=None, body=b""):
128	        request = f"{method} {path} HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: localhost\r\n"
129	        request += "".join(f"{key}: {value}\r\n" for key, value in (headers or {}).items())
130	        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", self.port), timeout=5) as connection:
131	            connection.sendall(request.encode("ascii") + b"\r\n" + body)
132	            chunks = []
133	            while True:
134	                chunk = connection.recv(65536)
135	                if not chunk:
136	                    break
137	                chunks.append(chunk)
138	        head, payload = b"".join(chunks).split(b"\r\n\r\n", 1)
139	        lines = head.split(b"\r\n")
140	        headers = dict(line.decode("latin-1").split(": ", 1) for line in lines[1:])
141	        return check_wire(int(lines[0].split()[1]), headers, payload)
142	
143	    def token(self):
144	        reply = self.call("POST", "/v1/tokens", headers=ADMIN)
145	        assert reply[0] == 201
146	        return json.loads(reply[2])["token"]
147	
148	    def auth(self, token=None):
149	        return {"Authorization": "Bearer " + (token or self.token())}
150	
151	    def create(self, auth, slug="sample", url="https://example.test/a", **extra):
152	        value = {"url": url, **extra}
153	        if slug is not None:
154	            value["slug"] = slug
155	        return self.call("POST", "/v1/links", encode(value), auth)
156	
157	    def clock(self, now):
158	        reply = self.call("POST", "/v1/admin/clock", encode({"now": now}), ADMIN)
159	        assert (reply[0], reply[2]) == (200, encode({"now": now}))

161	    def stop(self, sig=None):
162	        if hasattr(self, "stop_seconds"):
163	            return self.stop_seconds
164	        running = self.process.poll() is None
165	        if sig is None:
166	            sig = signal.CTRL_BREAK_EVENT if os.name == "nt" else signal.SIGTERM
167	        started = time.monotonic()
168	        try:
169	            if running:
170	                self.process.send_signal(sig)
171	            self.process.wait(timeout=5)
172	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
173	            self.process.kill()
174	            self.process.wait(timeout=5)
175	            pytest.fail("server failed to exit within five seconds of its clean signal")
176	        finally:
177	            self.reader.join(timeout=2)
178	            self.process.stdout.close()
179	            self.stderr_file.close()
180	        self.stop_seconds = time.monotonic() - started
181	        assert running, ("server exited before its clean signal", self.process.returncode,
182	                         self.stderr_path.read_bytes())
183	        assert self.process.returncode == 0, self.stderr_path.read_bytes()
184	        assert self.stop_seconds < 5
185	        assert not self.reader.is_alive()
186	        assert self.lines == [self.ready_line], self.lines
187	        assert b"Traceback" not in self.stderr_path.read_bytes()
188	        return self.stop_seconds

222	    if signal_name == "SIGBREAK":

225	        sig = signal.CTRL_BREAK_EVENT
226	    else:

230	    api = processes()
231	    assert api.call("GET", "/healthz?ignored")[2] == b'{"status":"ok"}'
232	    auth = api.auth()

235	                 "\r\nContent-Length: 100\r\n\r\n{").encode("ascii")]
236	    connections = []
237	    try:
238	        for partial in partials:
239	            connection = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", api.port), timeout=5)
240	            connections.append(connection)
241	            connection.sendall(partial)
242	        # Acceptance of a later connection follows the three incomplete sockets.
243	        assert api.call("GET", "/healthz")[0] == 200

1	"""Argument parsing and lazy server/client dispatch."""
2	
3	import argparse
4	import os
5	
6	from .domain import APIError, parse_timestamp
7	
8	
9	def _nonempty(value):
10	    if not value:
11	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must not be empty")
12	    return value
13	
14	
15	def _port(value):
16	    number = int(value)
17	    if not 0 <= number <= 65535:
18	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be between 0 and 65535")
19	    return number
20	
21	
22	def _rate_limit(value):
23	    number = int(value)
24	    if number < 1:
25	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be at least 1")
26	    return number
27	
28	
29	def _timestamp(value):
30	    try:
31	        return parse_timestamp(value)
32	    except APIError as error:
33	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(error.message) from None
34	
35	
36	def _client_options(parser):
37	    # Suppressed defaults preserve options supplied before the token create leaf.
38	    parser.add_argument("--server", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
39	    parser.add_argument("--token", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
40	
41	
42	def _parser():
43	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="linkvault")
44	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
45	
46	    serve = commands.add_parser("serve")
47	    serve.add_argument("--db", required=True)
48	    serve.add_argument("--admin-key", required=True, type=_nonempty)
49	    serve.add_argument("--port", type=_port, default=8000)
50	    serve.add_argument("--rate-limit", type=_rate_limit, default=60)
51	    serve.add_argument("--fake-clock", type=_timestamp)
52	
53	    token = commands.add_parser("token")
54	    _client_options(token)
55	    token_commands = token.add_subparsers(dest="token_command", required=True)
56	    create = token_commands.add_parser("create")
57	    _client_options(create)
58	    create.add_argument("--admin-key", required=True, type=_nonempty)
59	
60	    shorten = commands.add_parser("shorten")
61	    _client_options(shorten)
62	    shorten.add_argument("url")
63	    shorten.add_argument("--slug")
64	    shorten.add_argument("--expires-in", type=int)
65	
66	    listing = commands.add_parser("list")
67	    _client_options(listing)
68	    for name in ("stats", "delete"):
69	        command = commands.add_parser(name)
70	        _client_options(command)
71	        command.add_argument("slug")
72	    return parser
73	
74	
75	def main(argv=None):
76	    parser = _parser()
77	    try:
78	        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
79	        if args.command != "serve":
80	            args.server = getattr(args, "server", os.environ.get("LINKVAULT_SERVER"))
81	            args.token = getattr(args, "token", os.environ.get("LINKVAULT_TOKEN"))
82	            if not args.server:
83	                parser.error("--server or LINKVAULT_SERVER is required")
84	            if args.command != "token" and not args.token:
85	                parser.error("--token or LINKVAULT_TOKEN is required")
86	    except SystemExit as error:
87	        return error.code
88	
89	    if args.command == "serve":
90	        from . import server
91	
92	        return server.run(args)
93	
94	    from . import client
95	
96	    return client.run(args)

1	"""One locked SQLite connection; owners are authenticated token digests."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import hashlib
6	import re
7	import secrets
8	import sqlite3
9	import threading
10	
11	from .domain import APIError, format_timestamp, validate_create
12	
13	
14	_SCHEMA = """
15	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
16	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
17	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
18	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
19	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
20	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
21	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
22	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
23	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
24	  expires_at INTEGER,
25	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
26	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
27	"""
28	_ALPHABET = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
29	_TOKEN = re.compile(r"lv_[0-9a-f]{32}")
30	
31	
32	def _digest(token: str) -> str:
33	    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
34	
35	
36	def _link(row: sqlite3.Row, base_url: str) -> dict:
37	    return {
38	        "slug": row["slug"],
39	        "url": row["url"],
40	        "short_url": f"{base_url}/{row['slug']}",
41	        "created_at": format_timestamp(row["created_at"]),
42	        "expires_at": (format_timestamp(row["expires_at"])
43	                       if row["expires_at"] is not None else None),
44	        "clicks": row["clicks"],
45	        "last_clicked_at": (format_timestamp(row["last_clicked_at"])
46	                            if row["last_clicked_at"] is not None else None),
47	    }
48	
49	
50	class Storage:
51	    def __init__(self, path: str):
52	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
53	        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
54	        with self._lock:
55	            try:
56	                self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
57	                self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
58	                self._conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
59	                self._conn.commit()
60	            except Exception:
61	                self._conn.close()
62	                raise
63	
64	    def close(self) -> None:
65	        with self._lock:
66	            self._conn.close()
67	
68	    def issue_token(self, now: int) -> dict:
69	        token = "lv_" + secrets.token_hex(16)
70	        with self._lock, self._conn:
71	            self._conn.execute(
72	                "INSERT INTO tokens (token_hash, created_at) VALUES (?, ?)",
73	                (_digest(token), now),
74	            )
75	        return {"token": token, "created_at": format_timestamp(now)}
76	
77	    def authenticate(self, token: str) -> str:
78	        if not isinstance(token, str) or _TOKEN.fullmatch(token) is None:
79	            raise APIError(401, "unauthorized", "Invalid token")
80	        token_hash = _digest(token)
81	        with self._lock:
82	            exists = self._conn.execute(
83	                "SELECT 1 FROM tokens WHERE token_hash = ?", (token_hash,),
84	            ).fetchone()
85	        if exists is None:
86	            raise APIError(401, "unauthorized", "Invalid token")
87	        return token_hash
88	
89	    def create_link(self, token_hash: str, body: dict, now: int, base_url: str) -> dict:
90	        validate_create(body)
91	        with self._lock, self._conn:
92	            if "slug" in body:
93	                slug = body["slug"]
94	                if slug == "healthz" or self._exists(slug):
95	                    raise APIError(409, "slug_taken", "Slug is taken")
96	            else:
97	                for _ in range(5):
98	                    slug = "".join(secrets.choice(_ALPHABET) for _ in range(7))
99	                    if slug != "healthz" and not self._exists(slug):
100	                        break
101	                else:
102	                    raise APIError(500, "internal", "Could not generate a free slug")
103	            expires_at = now + body["expires_in"] if "expires_in" in body else None
104	            self._conn.execute(
105	                "INSERT INTO links (slug, url, token_hash, created_at, expires_at) "
106	                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
107	                (slug, body["url"], token_hash, now, expires_at),
108	            )
109	            row = self._conn.execute("SELECT * FROM links WHERE slug = ?", (slug,)).fetchone()
110	        return _link(row, base_url)
111	
112	    def _exists(self, slug: str) -> bool:
113	        """Called only while holding the connection lock."""
114	        return self._conn.execute(
115	            "SELECT 1 FROM links WHERE slug = ?", (slug,),
116	        ).fetchone() is not None
117	
118	    def list_links(self, token_hash: str, base_url: str) -> dict:
119	        with self._lock:
120	            rows = self._conn.execute(
121	                "SELECT * FROM links WHERE token_hash = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC, slug ASC",
122	                (token_hash,),
123	            ).fetchall()
124	        return {"links": [_link(row, base_url) for row in rows]}
125	
126	    def get_link(self, token_hash: str, slug: str, base_url: str) -> dict:
127	        with self._lock:
128	            row = self._conn.execute(
129	                "SELECT * FROM links WHERE token_hash = ? AND slug = ?", (token_hash, slug),
130	            ).fetchone()
131	        if row is None:
132	            raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Link not found")
133	        return _link(row, base_url)
134	
135	    def delete_link(self, token_hash: str, slug: str) -> None:
136	        with self._lock, self._conn:
137	            deleted = self._conn.execute(
138	                "DELETE FROM links WHERE token_hash = ? AND slug = ?", (token_hash, slug),
139	            ).rowcount
140	            if not deleted:
141	                raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Link not found")
142	
143	    def resolve(self, slug: str, now: int) -> str:
144	        with self._lock, self._conn:
145	            row = self._conn.execute(
146	                "SELECT url, expires_at FROM links WHERE slug = ?", (slug,),
147	            ).fetchone()
148	            if row is None:
149	                raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Link not found")
150	            if row["expires_at"] is not None and now >= row["expires_at"]:
151	                raise APIError(410, "gone", "Link expired")
152	            self._conn.execute(
153	                "UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?",
154	                (now, slug),
155	            )
156	            return row["url"]

20	- [kanban.md](kanban.md): mutable single source for Backlog/Ready/In Progress/Blocked/In Review/Done; validate each move.

23	## Implementation/test paths (planned, created by workers)
24	
25	`linkvault/__init__.py`, `__main__.py`, `domain.py`, `storage.py`, `server.py`, `cli.py`, `client.py` are minimal recommended decomposition. Exact stdlib-only public entry point is `python -m linkvault`. Task notes may document smaller internal interfaces without changing contract.

27	Focused tests: `tests/test_domain.py`, `tests/test_storage.py`, `tests/test_server.py`, `tests/test_client.py`; integrated `tests/test_acceptance.py`. Run commands in each task before advancing and whole `python -m pytest -q` at integration. Record interpreter/version/platform, count/pass/fail/skip, actual command and source revision/fingerprint. Existing usable >=3.11 preferred; default3.9 execution is explicitly below-target, not supported-runtime proof. No installation authorized.

31	Current exported plugin root: `/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/.eval-cfg-20261102T053248Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration`. Run Python scripts `validate-task-schema.py`, `validate-kanban.py`, `validate-planning-folder.py` with `--path docs/spec-001-feature/`. After every provisional Done run `check-dod.py --path docs/spec-001-feature/ --task Tx` in same step; move back on failure. Run `check-commit.py --message ...` before every commit. Frozen spec/plan/draft/references/task bodies must not change during implementation; use notes/handoff for integration decisions, preserve baseline hashes.
32	
33	All phases require independent reviewer subagent, per-task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE with reviewer ID before advancement. Last phase included. Final acceptance additionally requires explicit `impl-review`, approved fixes via coder and re-review until PASS. Orchestrator does not edit product code/tests. Never push/amend/force/bypass hooks. Stop and checkpoint on Blocked or budget reserve/invalid/exhausted. Stage budget checks include absolute deadline and reserve in every brief and before/after waits.

37	Official Python 3.11 http.server, socketserver, signal, socket, sqlite3, urllib.parse/request/error, datetime and stdtypes sources are linked in specification. Research uses stable official semantics; none overrides contract.

## HTTP Wire Contract & Server Lifecycle Review

**Scope:** Final `impl-review` lane 2 for candidate `7e52c817def50c793a601fe9b2f12361a081c99d`, against the authoritative [contract](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/contract.md>).

- [Server implementation](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/linkvault/server.py>)
- [Focused HTTP/lifecycle tests](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/tests/test_server.py>)
- Immediate Storage, Clock and CLI interfaces, plus relevant process-acceptance assertions.

**Hash basis:** The [23-entry review manifest](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/impl-review-inputs.json>) records server SHA-256 `8f8f6611b7361eb88f51ef550f3e3189eb705b0bed79022d3ebed096c17bc337` and focused-test SHA-256 `289bda31b1b23da4f81e66d571c758992d1550103a44b15d691b3441c4d90782`. Both agree with the retained validation ledgers. Current-tree hash verification is parent-supplied.

Accepted task/phase evidence remains applicable. **No task was reopened:** no concrete defect, contradictory evidence or changed dependency was found.

### Required Findings — Must Fix

**None.** No issue met the ≥80-confidence reporting threshold.

### Review Results

| Assigned criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| Raw method/path/query and slug matching | Exact dispatch uses the original request line, removes only the query, avoids stdlib leading-slash normalization, and routes unlisted extension methods to JSON 404. Focused raw-request cases cover these distinctions. |
| Failure precedence and admin enabledness | Route → auth → rate → size → JSON → validation → state ordering is preserved across interfaces. Disabled clock routing fails before authentication; bypass routes do not consume quota. |
| Exact response wire behavior | Shared serialization preserves required JSON encoding and key order, explicit byte lengths and JSON Content-Type. DELETE/redirect bodies are empty with length zero. Independent acceptance assertions supplement the focused tests’ shared encoder. |
| Framing and 8192-byte cap | Oversized recognized requests return 413/close before body reads. Decimal length is normalized and bounded **before** integer conversion; conversion receives at most four digits. The accepted Python ≥3.11 digit-cap defect remains resolved. |
| Startup and drained shutdown | Loopback binding precedes flushed readiness. Startup failures return 3. Shutdown stops serving, interrupts active sockets, joins handlers, then closes storage. Retained SIGINT/SIGTERM cases exercise idle, partial-header and partial-body connections. |
| Evidence demonstrates assigned outcomes | Assertions cover wire bytes, precedence, state transitions, concurrency and lifecycle outcomes—not merely successful command execution. No hidden mandatory gap was identified under the approved available-host validation policy. |

### Test Evidence Reused

- [Whole-suite output](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/evidence/t4/whole.stdout.log>): **560 passed, 2 Windows-only skips**, 37.58 s.

- [Compilation ledger](</Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c2-linkvault-20261102T053248Z/docs/spec-001-feature/evidence/t4/compile.json>): exit **0**, seven package sources.

### Nonblocking Warnings

- All execution evidence is **Python 3.9.6 on macOS**, below the required runtime. Python ≥3.11 and Windows/Linux execution remain unproved. The frozen validation plan explicitly permits this disclosed fallback; these results must not be relabeled supported-runtime/platform proof.
- Unicode `Location` transport retains Latin-1 bytes where encodable and UTF-8 otherwise. Raw-byte tests verify that policy, but universal client interoperability is not established because the contract specifies no Unicode header charset.
- The previously disclosed timestamp-plus-expiry overflow boundary remains undefined by the contract; it is not reopened as a new HTTP requirement.

When an authorized supported runtime/platform becomes available, rerun the existing validation and signal cases without changing requirements.

This was read-only review and evidence inspection. No commands were executed, tests rerun, hashes independently recomputed or files edited in this lane.
